quote: O let the soul her slumbers break, / Let thought be quickened, and awake, / Awake to see / How soon this life is past and gone, / And death comes softly stealing on, / How silently!
source: Jorge Manrique, Coplas por la muerte de su padre, stanza I, lines 1 to 6 (trans. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, 1833)

evidence.where: the 1833 first edition, read in the Internet Archive scan of the Boston Public Library (Ticknor) copy, and compared with the Project Gutenberg Complete Poetical Works
evidence.edition: Coplas de Don Jorge Manrique, translated from the Spanish (Boston: Allen and Ticknor, 1833), first edition per BAL 12054
evidence.locator: Stanzas composed by Don Jorge Manrique on the death of his father Don Rodrigo, stanza I, lines 1 to 6. The 1833 text reads awake, with a comma at the end of line 2; the later collected text in Gutenberg 1365 reads awake; with a semicolon

reason: Read verbatim in the 1833 first edition. The wording is identical to the proposal except one punctuation mark: the 1833 printing has a comma after awake where later collected editions have a semicolon, so the line ships in the wording of the edition the source names.
